title: Pulsed Sonidegib for Better Tolerability in Gorlin Syndrome and Multiple BCC
official: A Phase II Study of Sonidegib in Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome (Gorlin) Syndrome and Sporadic BCC Patients in EADO Stage IIb
summary:
The rare hereditary nevus-associated basal cell carcinoma syndrome (NBCCS), also known as Gorlin syndrome, is characterized by the development of hundreds of basal cell carcinomas (BCCs) over the course of an affected individual's lifetime and by an increased risk of medulloblastomas and rhabdomyosarcomas. Some non-NBCCS patients with multiple BCC lesions present similar clinical challenges (EADO stage IIb). Collectively, these patients represent a particularly difficult population to treat due to the frequent need for surgical removal of early-stage lesions and the contraindication to radiation therapy. Considering the properties of sonidegib and the advantages of a personalized treatment plan, we propose a Phase II study in the NBCCS population and in sporadic patients with EADO Stage IIb BCC to evaluate the efficacy and safety of sonidegib administered at intermittent doses.

The study consists of 2 phases:

* a 16-week full-dose phase (induction)
* a 24-week intermittent-dose phase (maintenance)

After confirmation of inclusion/exclusion criteria, the patient will be enrolled in the full-dose phase with administration of 200 mg of sonidegib daily for 16 weeks. In this phase, dose reduction and discontinuation of treatment may be employed in accordance with clinical practice (see section on Dose Reduction and Discontinuation of Treatment). After 16 weeks, subjects who achieve at least a partial response according to the RECIST criteria (see Appendix E) will enter the intermittent administration phase. In this phase, subjects will receive treatment in cycles lasting 4 weeks: they will take 200 mg of sonidegib daily for 2 weeks, followed by a 2-week drug-free interval. The maintenance phase will continue until disease progression, the occurrence of intolerable adverse events, or at the discretion of the subject and physician. After 24 weeks of the maintenance phase, if no progression is detected and no permanent discontinuation of treatment has occurred, subjects may continue therapy with sonidegib according to standard clinical practice. The decision to continue treatment with sonidegib will be a shared decision between the patient and the physician. After 24 weeks of the maintenance phase, subjects will enter the safety follow-up phase of the study.

The objectives of the study are:

Primary: treatment adherence in a population of NBCCS / sporadic BCC patients with EADO stage IIb disease treated for 16 weeks with daily sonidegib followed by an intermittent dosing regimen for the subsequent 24 weeks.

Secondary:

* The activity of a pulsed sonidegib regimen, following 16 weeks of sonidegib administered daily
* The efficacy of a pulsed sonidegib regimen, following 16 weeks of sonidegib administered daily
* The safety of a pulsed sonidegib regimen following 16 weeks of daily sonidegib administration
* The impact on quality of life of a pulsed sonidegib regimen following 16 weeks of daily sonidegib administration
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:1. Written signed informed consent for the trial. 2. Age ≥ 18 years, on day of signing informed consent. 3. One of the following conditions a. Subject with established diagnosis of NBCCS. b. Subject with common\\sporadic BCC.

4\. Clinical stage IIB according to EADO Classification \[Very high number of common BCC (\>10) or multiple complex BCC (\> 5) in the setting of apparently sporadic cases or in Gorlin syndrome. When at least 1 of the multiple BCC can be classified III or IV, the patient will be classified accordingly, and not IIB\].

5\. Being deemed difficult to treat: not amenable for surgery or RT after the evaluation of a multidisciplinary team involving at least a dermatologist and a medical oncologist and therefore eligible for HHI therapy.

6\. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1. 7. Demonstrate adequate organ function as defined in appendix D. All screening labs should be performed within 15 days of treatment initiation.

8\. Female subjects of childbearing potential should have a negative urine or serum pregnancy test within 72 hours prior to receiving the first dose of study medication. If the urine test is positive or cannot be confirmed as negative, a serum pregnancy test will be required.

9\. Female subjects of childbearing potential must be willing to use an adequate method of contraception for the course of the study through 20 months after the last dose of study medication. Note: Abstinence is acceptable if this is the usual lifestyle and preferred contraception for the subject.

10\. Female subjects must agree to not breastfeed during the study and for 20 months after the last dose of study treatment.

11\. Male subjects of childbearing potential must agree to use an adequate method of contraception starting with the first dose of study therapy through 20 months after the last dose of study therapy. Note: Abstinence is acceptable if this is the usual lifestyle and preferred contraception for the subject.

12\. Agreement not to donate blood or blood products during the study and for at least 180 days after the last dose was received.

13\. For male patients, agreement not to donate sperm during treatment and for 180 days after the last dose was received.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Distant metastatic disease (M1), visceral and/or distant nodal.
2. Prior HHI therapy in the last 2 years.
3. Received previous systemic treatment for BCC; local therapy (e.g.imiquimod) are allowed.
4. Currently participating and receiving study therapy or has participated in a study of an investigational agent and received study therapy or used an investigational device within 4 weeks of the first dose of treatment.
5. Hypersensitivity to sonidegib or any of its excipients.
6. Solid malignancy within 5 years of the projected enrolment date, or hematologic malignancy (excluding untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia) at any time; exceptions include basal cell carcinoma of the skin or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin that has undergone potentially curative therapy or curatively resected in situ cervical and/or breast cancers, as well as low grade prostate cancers as described below: a. Untreated Stage T1c or T2a with a Gleason score \< 6 and a PSA (\< 2 ng/ml) that has been stable for the past year prior to trial allocation on active surveillance, or b. Stage T1c or T2a with a Gleason score of \< 6 and PSA level \< 10 ng/ml that has been definitively treated.
7. Active infection requiring systemic therapy.
8. Inability or unwillingness to swallow capsules.
9. History or current evidence of any condition, therapy, or laboratory abnormality that might confound the results of the trial, interfere with the subject's participation for the full duration of the trial, or is not in the best interest of the subject to participate, in the opinion of the treating investigator.
10. Known psychiatric or substance abuse disorders that would interfere with cooperation with the requirements of the trial.
11. Pregnant, breastfeeding or expecting to conceive or father children within the projected duration of the trial, starting with the pre-screening or screening visit through 120 days after the last dose of trial treatment.
12. Received a live vaccine within 30 days of planned start of study therapy. a. Note: Seasonal influenza vaccines for injection are generally inactivated flu vaccines and are allowed; however intranasal influenza vaccines (e.g., Flu-Mist®) are live attenuated vaccines, and are not allowed.
